note: The only core fit in this batch and close to the textbook case. An endodontist working as an independent contractor is precisely the 'physician or equivalent' the stated ICP names, and income was never in question — she committed $3,000 on the call and treated the rest as a card-timing exercise. She is emphatically not the excluded profile: lean, three Boston Marathons, a six-minute personal record in April. And the good-to-great framing is her own — 'I kind of just want to see how strong I can get and how it can translate into other aspects of my life', with the aesthetic outcome explicitly a bonus she does not expect. Neglected health is the one criterion needing a caveat: she is far better resourced on health than the ICP imagines, seeing a physical therapist weekly, but strength training and nutrition are genuinely the underinvested dimensions and she says so herself. The finding worth carrying forward is what this pairing exposes. The stated ICP scores her a perfect five out of five, and she is simultaneously the highest clinical risk in the batch — five months from a torn labrum and torn ATFL, still in active rehabilitation, sold snatches with no clearance sought. That is the criterion the ICP does not have.
